title: Conformance as a Distribution: Delegation Contracts, Error Budgets, and the Allocation of Evaluation Authority in Use-Based AI Regulation
abstract: arXiv:2610.33112v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Use-based AI regulation assigns obligations by deployment risk but lacks an evidentiary object to carry them. A benchmark score is a property of a model; conformance of a deployment is a failure rate under a declared distribution of contexts, bounded by a scope and subject to expiry. We take the delegation contract of earlier work (frozen configuration, scoped claim, executable revision rule) and study it under strategic play between a deployer, an auditor, and an enforcement point. We ask whether a declared context mixture can be made truthful; whether an audit can be unbiased against a system that detects evaluation traffic; whether a certification error budget can sustain a long-lived deployment; whether an aggregate audit can support a per-subgroup guarantee; and whether an incident metric that counts system failures but not fallback costs ranks arrangements correctly. For each we give a mechanism and a proposition: a proper-scoring

translated_title: 一致性作为一种分布：委托合同、错误预算与基于用途的AI监管中评估权威的分配
translated_abstract: 基于用途的AI监管根据部署风险来分配义务，但缺乏承载这些义务的证据对象。基准测试分数是模型的一种属性；而部署的一致性则是在已声明的情境分布下的失败率，受范围限定并具有时效性。我们采用先前工作中的委托合同（冻结配置、范围化声明、可执行的修订规则），并在部署方、审计方与执法点三者之间的策略性博弈中对其进行研究。我们探讨：已声明的情境混合能否被约束为真实；面对能够检测出评估流量的系统，审计能否保持无偏；认证错误预算能否支撑长期存续的部署；总体审计能否支持针对各子群体的保证；以及一个只统计系统失败而不计回退成本的事件指标能否正确地对各种安排进行排序。针对每一个问题，我们给出一个机制和一个命题：一个适当评分……
tldr: 该论文将基于用途的AI监管中的部署合规性重新定义为在已声明情境分布下的失败率而非模型属性，并针对部署方、审计方与执法点之间的策略博弈，给出可约束真实声明、无偏审计、可持续错误预算与子群体保证等机制，为监管提供可执行的证据对象。
en_tdlr: The paper reframes deployment conformance in use-based AI regulation as a failure rate under a declared context distribution, and designs mechanisms—truthful context mixtures, detection-robust audits, sustainable error budgets, and per-subgroup guarantees—to allocate evaluation authority among deployers, auditors, and enforcement points under strategic play.
